Macrons

Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

care verb and noun

look after

also look after, take care of, care for, mind the children, attend to, tend

classical

Cic. Att. 2.2.1: cūrā, amābō tē, Cicerōnem nostrum
Cato, Agr. 54: bovēs bene cūrāre

cūrō, cūrāre, cūrāvī, cūrātum

verb, first conjugation

look after, take care of

With an accusative: a child, a patient, animals, plants. Corpus or sē cūrāre is to look after oneself with food and rest. For Cūrā ut valeās see take care.

Other words

  • cūra, cūrae f. — care, looking after

    noun, first declension · classical · Verg. A. 1.646: omnis in Ascaniō cārī stat cūra parentis; Plaut. Men. 897: cum cūrā magnā cūrābō

    Also worry and concern (see care, about something).

Examples

  • cūrā, amābō tē, Cicerōnem nostrum

    Look after our little Cicero, please.Cic. Att. 2.2.1

  • ita ego eum cum cūrā magnā cūrābō tibi

    So I’ll look after him for you with great care.Plaut. Men. 897

  • nunc corpora cūrāre tempus est

    Now it’s time for food and rest.Liv. 21.54.2

  • omnis in Ascaniō cārī stat cūra parentis

    All his loving father’s care is fixed on Ascanius.Verg. A. 1.646

See also take care, nanny, day care, care.
